stem.text: Sand is added to a pile at a rate modeled by the differentiable function \( S \), where \( S(t) \) is measured in cubic feet per hour and \( t \) is measured in hours for \( 0 \le t \le 7 \). At time \( t = 0 \) the pile contains 40 cubic feet of sand. Selected values of \( S(t) \) are given in the table. \( \begin{array}{c|cccc} t \text{ (hours)} & 0 & 2 & 3 & 7 \\ \hline S(t) \text{ (cubic feet per hour)} & 5 & 8 & 6 & 10 \end{array} \)

parts.prompt: Use a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by the table to approximate \( \int_{0}^{7} S(t)\,dt \). Show the computations that lead to your answer.

worked_solution.text: Each trapezoid is its width times the average of its two end values.

points.criterion: Writes a trapezoidal sum of three terms, each a width times an average of two table values, with at least five of the six factors correct.
Gives the value 52 with the supporting products present.

parts.prompt: Use your answer from part (a) to approximate the amount of sand in the pile at time \( t = 7 \) hours.

worked_solution.text: Add the initial amount to the accumulated change.

points.criterion: Adds the initial 40 cubic feet to the integral approximation from part (a), consistent with that answer.
